messages.author: da33143a8db60ce8
messages.subject: tried to install pystan
parts:
Hi, just for laffs I decided to install pystan. I started by installing Python, I wasn’t sure which version to use so I tried 2.7. Then I got stuck: I don’t know how to install Cython or NumPy. So I jumped over to here:
pip install pystan
But in Python I got the following error:

—

>>> pip install pystan
SyntaxError: invalid syntax

—

Then I tried the other way and got this:

—

>>> wget https://pypi.python.org/packages/source/p/pystan/pystan-2.7.0.0.tar.gz
# alternatively, use curl, or a web browser
tar zxvf pystan-2.7.0.0.tar.gz
cd pystan-2.7.0.0
python setup.py install
cd .. # change out of the source directory before importing pystan

SyntaxError: invalid syntax

—

I’m sure I’m just doing something dumb—I don’t know python at all and have never ever used it—I just thought it might be helpful for people to realize that, to a complete newbie, the instructions aren’t quite enough.

A

messages.author: c4d395346152354a
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] tried to install pystan
parts:
A more detailed set of instructions:

  1. Download Anaconda: http://continuum.io/downloads
  2. Install it (on mac) using bash: bash Anaconda-2.3.0-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
  3. it will create a anaconda folder in your home directory. Yes yes to appending anaconda to your PATH
  4. restart your terminal
1. install numpy and cython with conda install numpy cython

1. install latest pystan with pip install pystan (if you conda install pystan it is still on ver 2.6)
​

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] tried to install pystan
parts:
From previous discussions with users who aren't computer scientists,
the big blocking point is using unix shells in the first place.
So instructions like "use bash" are met with replies like "what's bash?"
and then "how do I open the bash application"? Similarly, "what's
the terminal" and "how do I start it?" When you say, "use Spotlight,"
it's met with "what's Spotlight?". This is why RStudio, an IDE for R
that makes using R feel like using a Microsoft product are so popular.
Is there an equivalent for Python?

- Bob

Thanks, by the way! I think that's a good start and if
the instructions aren't at least this detailed, they should
be updated so they are.

I've been using unix since the mid-80s and I was never
able to install Python a few years ago because of all the
dependencies into Fortran and other compilers that didn't
come standard on Windows or Mac OSX. I wound up using Enthought
because they provided an installer that just worked. But it
made me feel dirty because of the IP restrictions.

- Bob

On Aug 2, 2015, at 11:25 PM, Daniel Chen <chend...@gmail.com> wrote:

There's a PR up for more detailed instructions.

For windows just make sure you check off the box that makes anaconda the default python.  It should be a double click and accept defaults for Macs

https://github.com/chendaniely/pystan/blob/feature/detailed-installation-instructions/installation_beginner.md




On Sun, Aug 2, 2015 at 7:21 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
No, I don’t know how to append to my path.  Also I don’t understand the relationship between Python and Anaconda!

> On Aug 2, 2015, at 7:17 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>
> Those were going to be the new instructions.  The problem
> with writing this kind of thing is where to stop the recursion.
> It'd be great if we could at least target you, but we won't know
> what you know until you try it.
>
> Do you know how to append to your path?
>
> I'm unclear on whether the 5th and 6th steps need to be done
> from the terminal or from within Python.
>
> - Bob
>
>
>> On Aug 2, 2015, at 6:59 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>>
>> OK, I guess I’ll wait until the updated instructions are posted on the website.  That will probably be more effective than me getting stuck on each step in this way!  I don’t even understand what it means to download Anaconda, given that I earlier downloaded Python, also I don’t understand why Python has a version number and Anaconda doesn’t . . . .really just too much.
>>
>> The reason why I was doing this was because Zacky knows Python (a little) so I wanted to show him Stan. . . .
>>
>>> On Aug 2, 2015, at 6:49 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:
>>>
>>> You need to run it from the directory in which it downloaded
>>> or provide the whole path.
>>>
>>> - Bob
>>>
>>>> On Aug 2, 2015, at 6:34 PM, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>>>>
>>>> Sorry, but these instructions didn’t work.  I did Step 1.  But then when I opened up a terminal window, I couldn’t do step 2:
>>>>
>>>> Last login: Sun Jul 19 18:24:16 on console
>>>> Andrews-MacBook-Pro:~ andrew$ bash Anaconda-2.3.0-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
>>>> bash: Anaconda-2.3.0-MacOSX-x86_64.sh: No such file or directory
>>>> Andrews-MacBook-Pro:~ andrew$
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>
>>>>> On Aug 2, 2015, at 1:41 PM, Daniel Chen <chend...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>>
>>>>> A more detailed set of instructions:
>>>>>
>>>>>   • Download Anaconda: http://continuum.io/downloads
>>>>>   • Install it (on mac) using bash: bash Anaconda-2.3.0-MacOSX-x86_64.sh
>>>>>   • it will create a anaconda folder in your home directory. Yes yes to appending anaconda to your PATH
>>>>>   • restart your terminal
>>>>>   • install numpy and cython with conda install numpy cython
>>>>>   • install latest pystan with pip install pystan (if you conda install pystan it is still on ver 2.6)
>>>>> ​
>>>>>
>>>>> On Sun, Aug 2, 2015 at 12:29 AM, <chend...@gmail.com> wrote:
>>>>> The simplest way would be to install the anaconda distribution of Python here http://continuum.io/downloads
>>>>>
>>>>> You can then install numpy and cython with "Vonda install numpy cython"
>>>>>
>>>>> Typed with opposable thumbs.
>>>>>
>>>>> On Aug 1, 2015, at 16:33, Andrew Gelman <gel...@stat.columbia.edu> wrote:
>>>>>
>>>>>> Hi, just for laffs I decided to install pystan. I started by installing Python, I wasn’t sure which version to use so I tried 2.7.  Then I got stuck:  I don’t know how to install Cython or NumPy.  So I jumped over to here:
>>>>>> pip install pystan
>>>>>> But in Python I got the following error:
>>>>>>
>>>>>> —
>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> pip install pystan
>>>>>> SyntaxError: invalid syntax
>>>>>>
>>>>>> —
>>>>>>
>>>>>> Then I tried the other way and got this:
>>>>>>
>>>>>> —
>>>>>>
>>>>>>>>> wget https://pypi.python.org/packages/source/p/pystan/pystan-2.7.0.0.tar.gz
>>>>>> # alternatively, use curl, or a web browser
>>>>>> tar zxvf pystan-2.7.0.0.tar.gz
>>>>>> cd pystan-2.7.0.0
>>>>>> python setup.py install
>>>>>> cd ..  # change out of the source directory before importing pystan
>>>>>>
>>>>>> SyntaxError: invalid syntax
>>>>>>
>>>>>> —
>>>>>>
>>>>>> I’m sure I’m just doing something dumb—I don’t know python at all and have never ever used it—I just thought it might be helpful for people to realize that, to a complete newbie, the instructions aren’t quite enough.
>>>>>>
>>>>>> A

parts:
Nice --- thanks Daniel. We'll be sure to cite you for
helping out.

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/issues/1526#issuecomment-127123552

I'm going to leave the Python instructions for Allen to review
and merge into PyStan, but if it works for Andrew, it should
be good to go. He's our canary in the coalmine :-)

- Bob
